# blyxt, Oct 13: a quiet feed, drafts that wait in Pub, and revisions

## The fragments that didn't stop

It started as a bug report: after the Pub and Sub topics were renamed, no blyg fragments seemed to arrive for a whole day. The last one received was vgr's "On Timeliness".

The trail went the other way. blyxt had polled every fifteen minutes throughout, with no errors. Every post vgr published on Oct 11 had been imported and sent to Sub, and Telegram confirmed each of those messages still existed. Lining his publish times up against the message ids settled it. "On Timeliness" went out at 6:15am on the 12th; the topics were renamed afterwards; then vgr published nothing for twenty-three hours. His next post landed at 4:49am this morning and reached Sub at 5:15, on the next poll.

So nothing broke. The rename fell inside a quiet stretch, and a quiet author and a broken poller look the same from inside the chat. Renaming a Telegram topic doesn't change its id, and the id is all blyxt keeps.

Two lessons came out of it. Following a blyg isn't just-in-time. Blygger 0.3 is pull-only, so a post shows up within one polling interval, not the moment it's published. And the poller should say it's alive. A configurable interval, and a "last checked" line in `/subscriptions`, are now on the list for an admin surface.

## Drafts: more than one way in, one point of publish

The other question was how text written outside Telegram, such as this post, should reach the blyg. Spec §5.7 already answers the protocol side. Generation is a studio act; where it ran isn't part of the claim; and text "produced by an external agent" is disclosed the same way as text generated in the studio. What the protocol doesn't settle is who presses publish. Until now that was always a gesture in Pub.

Over time a blyg might have several clients that write. The design keeps Telegram as the one place where writing becomes publishing:

- Another client (a script, an agent) can only submit a *draft* to an authenticated endpoint. Drafts are invisible to the protocol: no id, no feed entry, nothing public.
- The bot previews the draft in Pub. When the preview has to be cut short, the whole markdown comes attached as a file.
- Replying `/publish` makes it v1. Replying `/discard` hard-deletes it, which §9 allows because nothing was ever public.
- Once published, the preview message stands in for the post, so withdraw, republish and pin work on it the same way as on any other post.

A leaked token can therefore only propose. Nothing goes out without the owner's reply.

## Disclosure

A draft can declare itself generated. When it's published, the item document carries a `generated` entry naming the model and the time, plus any of this blyg's posts the text drew on. The body is wrapped in `blyg-tk-gen` in `content_html`. The endpoint keeps only those three fields and drops anything else a client sends, so a prompt can never reach the wire. A withdrawal endcap never carries the entry, and a republish brings it back along with the text.

One limit is deliberate for now. A generated draft can't quote another post. blyxt marks the whole body as generated, and a quote isn't generated text. Getting that right means marking spans rather than whole bodies.

## Revisions

Publishing a draft raised the next question straight away: how do you edit it? A post that started as a draft is tied to the bot's preview message, and Telegram doesn't let you edit a bot's message. A long post wouldn't fit in a message you could edit anyway.

The answer is a *revision draft*: a draft that names the post it revises. Its preview chains under the post in Pub. The preview shows the version bump, the changelog note, and which sections the revision changes. That summary stays in Pub, because §5.2 forbids a note from reproducing text that's withheld. `/publish` makes the next version of the same post, at the same address. The note goes into the changelog and in front of the title in the feed, so readers and followers can see the post changed and how. When Claude writes the note, rather than the author, the changelog entry says so with `"generated": true`. A revision written against an older version refuses to publish over a newer one.

The routine that came out of it: describe the changes in conversation, then Claude rewrites the post and sends it back as a revision. This section arrived that way, as v2 of the post.

## A devlog

Two posts in, this looks like it'll keep going: a log of blyxt, written by Claude from each session and published from Pub. The first post went out as v1 of this thread, and this revision extends it to cover the rest of the day. The next one is a review of Oct 12, the day L1 closed.
